messages:
mia (PM): quick one — we need to decide rollout sequencing + guardrails for adaptive-batching. customer pressure from two large PLG accounts, but this has perf/cost/regression risk. thoughts on RICE and canary strategy?
ashwin (eng): typo — ashwin :) suggest we treat as medium effort, high impact for throughput. RICE-wise: Reach=high, Impact=medium-high, Confidence=60%, Effort=4 -> score looks okay but depends on rollback speed.
ashwin (eng): key question: do we prioritize shipping to those paying customers asap or run broader canary first?
mia (PM): tradeoff — pushing direct to customers reduces churn risk but increases blast radius. prefer standard experiment sequence unless customer contract forces early access.
jorge (eng-ops): +1 for standard sequence. propose: internal -> 1% canary (non-prod tenants) -> 5% external beta -> 20% weighted rollout -> full. each step 24-48h guarded. fallback: automatic revert to stable batching=false model variant.
sara (data): need guardrail metrics: p95 latency, error-rate (5xx), token-cost delta, quality/regression on eval set (we have a 120-prompt smoke suite). define kill criteria: latency p95 > baseline + 30% or error-rate > 0.5% absolute for 15m or quality drop > 1.5% on eval.
liz (design): make sure UX signals included — slow streaming affects progress bars. add frontend metric: streaming-chunk-delay 95th. Also flag client-visible timeouts.
ashwin (eng): ops hooks: circuit breaker that automatically cuts new adaptive-batching requests when errors spike. Implement rate cap per-customer: max batch size 64 and max qps per customer. Also require KV cache warming for canary tenants.
jorge (eng-ops): rollout config draft:
```yaml
rollout:
  steps:
    - name: internal-canary
      pct: 0.5
      duration: 24h
    - name: public-canary
      pct: 5
      duration: 48h
    - name: weighted-ramp
      pct: 20
      duration: 72h
  fallback_variant: batching_disabled
  auto_kill_conditions:
    latency_p95_increase_pct: 30
    error_rate_absolute_pct: 0.5
    eval_quality_drop_pct: 1.5
```
mia (PM): do we need bespoke telemetry for the two paying customers if we gate them earlier?
sara (data): yes — add per-customer sampling at 100% for metrics and traces for the first 48h. need A/B tagging so we can run paired evals on their production prompts. power calc: to detect 1% absolute change with 80% power we need ~10k calls per arm. if those customers don't hit that, keep them in limited early access but don't call it an experiment.
ashwin (eng): scope negotiation: initial deliverable = server-side batching toggle + rollout controls + monitor hooks. defer per-customer tuning and UI toggles to post-launch. that keeps effort down.
liz (design): agree — minimize UI scope for v1. just an opt-in flag in console + basic telemetry surface.
qa-bot: TESTS: add integration test that simulates burst and ensures fallback triggers; add regression test against the 120-prompt suite.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy window available tonight 02:00-04:00 PST. auto-rollout toggles supported.
mia (PM): decision proposal: follow jorge's sequence, enforce sara's kill criteria, implement ashwin's circuit breakers and per-customer caps, ship minimal console opt-in. give early access to paying customers but only after public canary passes. target: canary deploy tonight -> 5% public canary after 48h -> ramp.
ashwin (eng): +1, will scope tasks and list risk items in PR.
jorge (eng-ops): +1, I'll add the rollout config to infra and set up auto-kill alerts + Slack pager if thresholds hit.
sara (data): I'll prepare the eval jobs and dashboards, and a quick-run script: `python eval/run_smoke.py --variant adaptive_batching --duration 24h`.
mia (PM): final note — if the contract requires earlier access, we'll do explicit customer-gated LTA and manual monitoring with on-call on standby. otherwise standard sequence. thanks all, I'll write up acceptance criteria and ship the RFC.
